STATUS: fail
SUMMARY: The change meets almost every criterion, and the boundary, single-use, and subclass probes all pass. One reproduced bug: a NaN `now` bypasses expiry entirely, so a token can be redeemed forever. The tests don't cover non-finite input, so they miss it.
FILES TOUCHED: none (probes and mutation copies live in /tmp/claude-0/-tmp-ff-eval-redteam-DIjm; the repo is unchanged apart from a git-ignored `shop/__pycache__/` that my imports may have created)
FINDINGS:
- [blocking] NaN disables expiry. `now - issued_at > RESET_TTL` is False when either side is NaN, so the token never expires. Reproduced: `t=issue_reset_token("u", now=0); redeem_reset_token(t, now=float('nan'))` returned `'u'` (expected TokenExpired). Also `issue_reset_token("u", now=float('nan'))` followed by `redeem_reset_token(t, now=1e9)` returned `'u'`. Fix: reject non-finite values, or write the check as `if not (now - record["issued_at"] <= RESET_TTL)`. Add a test for NaN.
- [minor] Single-use race not reproduced. Eight threads redeeming the same token with `sys.setswitchinterval(1e-6)` over 300 trials produced 0 double-successes. The check-then-set on `record["used"]` is still not atomic in principle; a lock would close it if the store is ever shared.
- [minor] Unreproduced: `redeem_reset_token` with an unhashable token (e.g. a list) raises TypeError rather than InvalidToken. The original code did the same, and the criteria don't cover it.
CHECKS:
- now=0 issue, redeem at 1800 → ok; at 1801 → TokenExpired (pass)
- float issue 1000.0: redeem 2800.0 → ok; 2800.5 → TokenExpired (pass)
- skew: issue 5000, redeem 1000 → ok (pass)
- two tokens, same user: using one leaves the other valid (pass)
- "" and None tokens → exact type InvalidToken (pass)
- used-and-expired (redeem at 99999) → TokenUsed (pass)
- expired redeem twice → TokenExpired both times, not marked used (pass)
- default `now` round-trip (pass); default-now token issued 1801 s ago → TokenExpired (pass)
- huge int timestamps 10**30 (pass)
- inf redeem → TokenExpired (pass)
- NaN redeem / NaN issue → both succeed (FAIL, see blocking)
- race: 8 threads × 300 trials, 0 double redeems (pass, unreproduced)
- Mutations on scratch copies, 11 real ones all killed by the suite: `>=` for `>`; `now or time.time()` at issue and at redeem; delete-on-redeem; no mark-used; expiry checked before used; mark-used before the expiry check; TTL 1799 and 1801; TokenExpired or TokenUsed not subclassing InvalidToken. The one survivor, a no-op control, is expected.
- grep: no other callers of the token API in the repo, so nothing was left un-updated.
- Checklist: follows the module-local exception pattern and tests/test_auth.py; README line is accurate; 1800/1801 are tested on both sides, with int, float and zero variants.
OPEN QUESTIONS: Should NaN be rejected with an error (e.g. ValueError), or treated as expired? Either way the fix needs a test. Also, can `shop/__pycache__/` be removed? My imports may have created it; it's git-ignored, so I left it in place.
